headline: Canal wall repairs at 145 Pawtucket Street and a sign and paint at 15-19 Merrimack Street approved
summary: A hearing on a temporary repair at 55 Kearney Square was continued for more information. Officers were elected, and a 2027 meeting schedule was accepted. A preliminary review of 15 townhomes at 520 Merrimack Street drew feedback from members.
decisions: Continued the hearing on a temporary repair at 55 Kearney Square until more information is available.
Approved repointing of the North Canal wall at 145 Pawtucket Street, with conditions on materials and a mock-up review before work starts.
Approved the illuminated sign and painting of the front facade at 15-19 Merrimack Street, with colors to be reviewed before work starts; rear paint to be reconsidered later.
Approved an order to appear for 478 Merrimack Street.
Approved the historic board schedule for 2027 as proposed.
Approved nominating George Vallares to continue as chair.
Approved nominating Geoffrey Harris as vice chair.
discussion: Valve Island repair timeline: Members asked how long the temporary repair would last and whether it would be inspected. The applicant gave no set time limit and said it could last for decades with maintenance.
Sign and paint at 15-19 Merrimack Street: Members said black paint on the front was too strong for the historic street. They suggested charcoal or warm gray instead.
Rear patio painting: Members said they wanted photos or a site visit before deciding whether to paint the older brick white. They raised concern that paint could trap moisture.
520 Merrimack Street townhomes: Members asked for a rendering in context and for the Merrimack Street side to look more like a front. They also questioned the shake siding.
Repair timelines for two properties: Property owners described plans for brick and window repairs and asked for time to pay for them. Members asked for timelines and regular updates.
